unit_sale_price.non_compliance_reason: Rule 6(11) limb (vii): '"Rs._ per litre" for pre-packaged commodities with net volume of the commodity more or equal to one litre.' The declared net quantity is 1 L, so the required basis is per litre; the pack declares a per-gram basis. The parenthesised (910 g) does not change the basis, which Rule 6(11) keys to the declared net volume. Rule 6(11) is a format rule and states no tolerance. Source: rules-corpus/LMPC-2011__amended-to-2021-10-31__maharashtra-compilation.pdf, Rule 6(11)(vii).

country_of_origin.non_compliance_reason: Rule 6(1)(aa) requires the name of the country of origin or manufacture or assembly 'in case of imported products'. Every address legible on this face is Indian and nothing on it indicates an imported product, so the obligation does not arise. Source: rules-corpus/LMPC-2011__amended-to-2021-10-31__maharashtra-compilation.pdf, Rule 6(1)(aa). There is no discrete country-of-origin statement on either face; the manufacturer address ends 'Maharashtra, India.', which is an address line and is not annotated as an origin declaration.

notes: Back label of the same bottle. Text rows slope with the bottle's curvature, so axis-aligned boxes cannot fit tightly; each was verified to contain its own declaration and not its neighbour. Both faces repeat the quantity, MRP and the wrongly based unit sale price. No reference object of known size is in frame, so no millimetre letter or numeral height is measurable and no Rule 7 Table-I finding is supportable. pdp.is_measurable is false and every height field is null. The sample verdict is REVIEW for that reason alone, independently of what the declarations show.
